layman_headline: The market is scared and the candidates are sketchy — staying on the sidelines for now.
layman_explanation: The overall crypto market is in a state of fear (27/100) and has been getting worse all week. Bitcoin is underperforming traditional stocks, which are hitting record highs, and Bitcoin dominance at 56.5% means altcoins are getting crushed even harder. The coins flagged as swing trade candidates are either tiny, illiquid tokens that have already surged (UB, BTW, PUMP) or beaten-down altcoins with no chart data and no clear bottom (LDO, KAITO, ETHFI). None of them offer a high-confidence setup with a clear stop-loss.
layman_action: Do nothing right now. Wait for fear to stabilize or reverse, and for a quality setup with proper technical confirmation to appear. Capital preservation is the priority in this environment.
expert_reasoning: Applying validated rules: Fear & Greed at 27 is just above the 25 threshold where Rule 3 says the outlook is genuinely ambiguous and HOLD is safest. The trend is worsening (yesterday was 25, week avg 26.7). BTC dominance at 56.5% is suppressing altcoin performance. Of the swing candidates, UB has the best chart score (+1.1) but RSI is neutral at 56, the risk/reward to nearest levels is only 0.49x (poor), and it's a micro-cap with no funding rate or volume data. BTW is RSI-overbought at 69 after a 79.7% weekly move — classic chase setup. LDO and KAITO have sharp dips (-20.6% and -25.1%) that could be mean-reversion plays, but with zero chart analysis data, no RSI readings, and no support levels identified, entering would be gambling. Per Rule 4 and my validated rules, I should not make a confident call when core data sources are missing for most candidates. The news flow is net bearish: BTC underperforming equities, longest Glassnode capitulation since FTX, Coldcard hack undermining custody narrative, and Ethereum's proposed issuance cut creating DeFi uncertainty.
risk_factors: Fear & Greed trending toward extreme fear (25 yesterday) — further downside likely if it breaks below 25
Bitcoin underperforming global equities suggests capital is rotating out of crypto, not in
Most swing candidates are illiquid micro-caps where a sudden sell-off could cause outsized losses with no exit liquidity
watch_list: Fear & Greed Index — if it drops below 25 into extreme fear, expect another leg down; if it bounces above 30, conditions may improve
Bitcoin vs. S&P 500 relative performance — crypto needs to stop lagging equities for any altcoin trade to work
ADA price action — up 18.5% on the week in a fearful market, could signal selective altcoin strength worth investigating
market_context: Crypto is in a fear-driven regime with Bitcoin at $64K lagging record-high equity markets. BTC dominance at 56.5% and the longest Glassnode capitulation signal since FTX suggest altcoins face continued headwinds until sentiment shifts.
context_banner: Fear is intensifying and Bitcoin is underperforming stocks — this is a capital preservation environment, not a swing trade environment.

key_signals.description: Fear & Greed at 27 with worsening trend (yesterday 25) signals market stress approaching extreme levels — per validated rules, ambiguous outlook favors holding.
Bitcoin failing to keep pace with record-high global equities indicates capital rotation away from crypto, a bearish macro signal.
Glassnode reports the longest Bitcoin price-metric capitulation since FTX, suggesting sustained seller exhaustion that hasn't yet found a floor.
Only two candidates have RSI data — UB at 56 (neutral) and BTW at 69 (overbought). Neither presents a classic oversold bounce setup which is the highest-reliability signal per track record.
Ethereum's proposed 54% staking reward cut threatens DeFi yield strategies, adding fundamental uncertainty to ETH-ecosystem tokens like LDO and ETHFI.
